chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan Al-Zayyat Al-Basri, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and I had a companion with me, and behold, he was in a room with padded walls, and upon him was a pink sheet, and he had trimmed his beard and applied kohl. So we asked him about some matters. When we arose, he said to me, 'O Hassan!' I said, 'At your service.' He said, 'When it is tomorrow, come to me, you and your companion.' So I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' When it was the next day, I entered upon him, and behold, he was in a room in which there was nothing except a mat, and upon him was a coarse shirt. Then he turned to my companion and said, 'O brother of the people of Basra! You came to me yesterday and I was in the wife's chamber, and yesterday was her day, and the room was her room, and the chattels were her chattels. So she adorned herself for me on the condition that I would adorn myself for her just as she adorned herself for me, so do not let anything enter your heart.' My companion said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, something had entered my heart, but as for now, by Allah, Allah has removed what was (in my heart), and I know that the truth is in what you said.'

key_terms.يَوْمَهَا: her day (her turn to be with the husband)

ai.seo_question: What is the lesson regarding marital etiquette and humility in this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s pedagogical use of *takhfif* (humility) and *tazyin* (adornment) to teach spiritual balance, specifically addressing the companion’s subtle jealousy or feeling of exclusion. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet’s household modeling healthy marital dynamics, where mutual beautification is a form of spiritual and social courtesy rather than vanity. The narrative serves as a practical lesson in purifying the heart from *hasad* (envy) through understanding the context of the Imam’s actions.
